scope: Plugin-based, independently audited cross-embodiment video Data Engine control plane and 100-accepted-hour capacity projection
summary: The CPU control plane, deterministic pilot planning, evidence-bound hard-gate audit state machine, capacity estimator, and responsive Data Engine demo work. A measured Wan infrastructure profile projects 13.2 days on 32 A800s for 100 accepted hours under explicit yield/utilization/overhead assumptions, but no 100-hour production campaign or one-hour multi-target scale pilot has run.

lessons: A reusable data factory needs immutable campaign state and typed plugin capabilities in addition to model adapters.
Independent hard-gate conjunction prevents attractive aggregate scores from admitting candidates that lose objects, motion, identity, or physical evidence.
Accepted-output estimates must model yield, utilization, non-generation overhead, audit labor, and storage; source-hour service throughput is a separate number.
limitations: The source manifest is an evaluation fixture whose training authorization must be confirmed before production use.
Shadow, Allegro, and Unitree files are lock descriptors; exact production asset bytes/revisions and the associated executor adapters are not yet resolved end to end.
The acceptance yield and multi-host scaling assumptions are not yet measured, and the 100-hour dataset has not been generated.
The current pilot claim scope is visual training data, not metric robot trajectories, persistent 3-D geometry, force/contact, or real-robot execution.
next_actions: Resolve authorized source splits and exact target asset revisions, then implement the source, retarget, generator, and auditor executor adapters behind the plugin ABI.
Run a one-hour multi-target A800 pilot and replace assumed yield, utilization, retry-tail, review, and storage values with measured distributions.
Promote only after independent gates pass across at least two scene/task groups; keep rejected morphology cases in the public benchmark.
